fix.behavior: An adapter run fault remains visible for the lifetime of the same drawn Client identity. Passive frame/render/resize results, new render revisions, and same-identity props updates do not clear it. Removing that Client node unmounts its React state; re-adding it creates a fresh Client identity instance. Environment epoch and site identity changes also remount through the existing React key.
fix.native_boundary: Native ui_client_fault records a failure against a drawn Client identity/version. Native eO.record([]) removes the identity entry; a later new record starts fresh. A renderVersions state-token change can also clear the Native failure marker, but Product currently has no authoritative equivalent state-token input and does not approximate it with render revision or props.

ranges.fact: Native Client fault tracker is keyed by site component/requestId and plugin/module/key. It stores a renderVersions-derived state token; record([]) deletes the tracked site. Same-key failure remains in the failure map while that token is unchanged.
Native ui.render begins tracking, awaits the hook, then records the accepted tree's Client keys; empty Client-key output clears that site's tracker.
Native ui.fault only reports a fault for a currently drawn Client and marks that identity/version as failed before dispatching the ui.fault hook.
ui_client_fault maps the request to the Native address {plugin, component, requestId, key, module} plus {phase, reason}.
The Native request handler calls E1e.clientFault and returns only whether the fault hook was handled; it does not directly reset the Client runtime.

native_source.known_gap: Product's local Client fault overlay has no authoritative mapping to Native's renderVersions state token. Current recovery is tied to real identity/site/environment remounts; state-token invalidation remains a follow-up boundary.

jsonl_persistence.path_scope: The TS recorder below is the headless turn-consumer path. The interactive transcript UI has a separate MSe/ASe recorder; it uses the same NE/transcript-writer path, but not TS.record().
jsonl_persistence.assistant_row_recording: With persistSession enabled, the headless consumer pushes each assistant row into its current transcript and calls TS.record() immediately on row arrival, after the query append side effect. That call is not awaited. Default record() selects all currently present rows: its default ge=false makes ANt(...,!ge) return the full list, including an assistant row whose stop_reason is still null. The TS cursor advances before NE() is called; the later message_delta record call does not select the same row again.
jsonl_persistence.query_append_scope: The main query wraps Xl in Ui.through (also through the observer wrapper). Ui.R accepts uuid/type rows of type user, assistant, attachment, or system and calls Xq when session.append is enabled and the running conversation is hookable. Thus the Tn user/tool-result row also passes through session.append before it is yielded to the headless consumer. Ui.through awaits that side effect, then yields the original event value; the hook projection is not substituted into the query event. The explicit r.appended(M) call remains a separate assistant-tool-use path, with Ui deduplicating the same row through its WeakSet.
jsonl_persistence.live_tool_result_recording: A tool_result is delivered as a user row. After Ui.through has completed the session.append side effect and yielded the original row, the headless user-row branch pushes it into the current transcript, awaits TS.record(), and only then continues consuming the stream. Therefore a completed tool result may be persisted while the provider stream is still open; the writer receives the original Native tool-result row, not the session.append projection.
jsonl_persistence.writer_path: TS.record() calls NE(), which normalizes the selected rows and invokes mi().insertMessageChain(). The writer awaits session-message reads, creates an outer transcript envelope by spreading each source row, then appendEntry enqueues that entry. The per-file queue preserves FIFO after admission; drain serializes with LM(entry) and appends the serialized chunk. Its scheduled flush interval is 100 ms.
jsonl_persistence.snapshot_limit: Static source proves an early write attempt, not whether its eventual JSONL bytes contain stop_reason:null or the terminal value. The row unwrap and transcript envelope are shallow spreads that preserve the nested message object; MessageDelta later mutates that same message object in the parser. Because the assistant record is not awaited and JSONL serialization happens later in the queue drain, either snapshot can win. The assistant and tool-result insertions also have async reads before queue admission, so this source alone does not guarantee their queue-admission order across separate record calls.
jsonl_persistence.interactive_cutoff: The interactive MSe.write path calls the same NE writer but passes isResponseInFlight to ANt. While that flag is true, ANt stops before the first assistant row whose stop_reason is null, so the incomplete trailing assistant row is held out of the persisted slice. ASe invokes MSe.record from transcript-snapshot and response-state effects. This pins the in-flight cutoff, not the precise scheduler moment when a post-delta row is flushed.
jsonl_persistence.tombstone_path: The headless tombstone branch calls TS.evict(message.uuid). If that row has passed the record cursor, TS.evict requests removeMessageByUuid; accepted fallback tombstones can therefore remove an already-recorded discarded assistant row. This does not establish that every error/decline path tombstones every earlier row.

stream_error.disposition: A final thrown model-stream error with no fallback-chain target reaches the model-error finalizer.
stream_error.completed_tools: The finalizer emits already completed results, takes any remaining finished results, and records ordinary user/tool-result rows.
stream_error.in_flight_tools: It discards the executor, aborts executing tools, leaves queued tasks unstarted, rebuilds the executor, and emits removals for in-progress IDs.
stream_error.unmatched_uses: It emits a synthetic cancelled tool_result for each remaining unpaired tool_use; the cancellation text warns that already-started effects may have happened.
stream_error.retry: This finalizer does not keep tool executions live for a model retry. A separate fallback-chain attempt uses abandonAttempt and its own tombstone/reset/abort path.

server_fallback.prior_results: je aliases ue.toolResults. Rows already handed off by earlier per-event Tn polls live in je; when a normal poll yields a result, xr appends its projected user rows after the yielded event is resumed. xr also preserves attachment rows and user rows returned by the normal tool-result projection. A tool that completed after the previous poll is not proven to be in je yet.

# Native Client state token and global render-version producers in 2.1.289

This note maps the `ui.render` version input used by Native Desktop Client
fault tracking. It is a static source audit of the pinned Claude Code 2.1.289
macOS arm64 executable, not a live Native UI run. The accompanying probe checks
the executable SHA, exact byte-window SHA values, and the producer call sites.

Run it with:

```sh
node scripts/tests/mods_ui_client_state_token_289_probe.mjs \
  /tmp/harness-claude-code-2.1.289-darwin-arm64
```

The binary SHA-256 is
`03d66745e3bb69ec727d66023696f3820bc0a00a8a5ba725eb6706d0c67cbe69`.
All source ranges below are zero-based, half-open byte offsets in that binary.

## Token inputs

Native initializes `renderVersions` as a map-backed store and names the global
version key `ui.render` (`Fv`). `kmn()` calls `E1t()` without a plugin, so it
increments that global key. `bh(key)` applies an immediate map update from
`old ?? 0` to `old + 1`.

For a site, the version signature is assembled as:

1. The current global `ui.render` counter.
2. For each currently matching `ui.render` plugin, its name and the counter for
   that plugin's site pace (`steady` or `live`), in the matched plugin order.
3. The site's `\0state` render-invalidation counter when it has committed at
   least one `$.state` read. The site key is `(surface, component, requestId)`;
   the counter advances after a relevant state mutation invalidates that site.

The implementation spells this as `EUe(state, site) = DY(Rh(state,
uUe(site), cS(site)), state, MD(site))`. `uUe` selects loaded modules matching
the `ui.render` event and all three site fields. The signature includes plugin
names as well as their counters, so adding a matching plugin with counter zero
or changing the matching order changes the signature too. `cS` uses the live
pace for terminal `AbovePrompt` while enabled, terminal `PromptHint`, and the
currently shown terminal `Pane`; other sites use steady pace.

`Rh` explicitly excludes the separate viewport key (`ui.render viewport`),
plugin live-counter entries, and state-key entries from its no-site aggregate
subscription signature. For a site signature it reads the global counter and
the ordered matching plugin names/counters; `DY` appends only that site's
state-invalidation counter. The viewport store is therefore a separate
invalidation input and is not the `Fv` global counter.

## Global `Fv` producers

The binary contains one `renderVersions` store initializer and one getter. Its
only two direct `HD().setState` call sites are the shared version incrementer
and the state-reader site-version updater. A full binary scan finds four
`kmn()` calls: one inside the shared Hooks cache invalidator, two after async
Hooks table resolution, and one in the directory-rehome path.

| Native operation | Source behavior | `Fv` effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hooks loaded-set commit (`J0t`'s `xe`) | After replacing the loaded module list, calls `Hae()` when the old or new loaded list is nonempty. `Hae()` calls `kmn()` before invalidating prompt-related caches. | One global increment on a committed nonempty set refresh/replacement. |
| Plugin unload (`FU`) | Calls `Hae()` after changing the loaded list, then awaits `Kae` table resolution and calls `kmn()` again. | Two distinct increments, one before and one after table resolution. |
| Plugin reload (`MLe`) | On the success path, waits for `Kae`, replaces the loaded module entry, then calls `Hae()`. Refusal/error paths return or throw before that commit. | One global increment after successful table resolution and replacement. |
| Hooks worker respawn (`sBt`) | Rebuilds the loaded modules, calls `Hae()`, awaits `Kae`, then calls `kmn()` again. | Two distinct increments around table resolution. |
| Working-directory rehome (`mit`) | After path/settings/skills rehome work, calls `kmn()` before emitting `tengu_cd_command`. This is not gated on `freshSession`; a rollback path that throws earlier does not reach it. | One global increment when the rehome flow reaches that point. |

`Hae()` also invalidates prompt caches, but its version effect is the global
`kmn()` call at its start. `ui.invalidate('ui.render')` is a separate route:
its Native bottom calls `E1t(plugin, 'steady')` and `E1t(plugin, 'live')`, so it
changes the matched plugin counters, not `Fv`.

There is no timer/debounce in `kmn`/`E1t`/`bh`: each reached call increments
the stored global counter. The unload and respawn paths intentionally reach
two increments separated by an `await`; no source evidence here says their
store notifications or downstream React work cannot batch. The probe reports
the counter writes, not renderer scheduling.

## State reads, folds, and render sampling

`$.state.get` records the current key version in the in-flight drawing scope.
After a non-aborted, identified `ui.render` completes, Native commits that
scope's read set. If a key changed while drawing, or a later state write
touches a committed read, Native marks the affected sites stale.

Ordinary stale-reader notifications use one pending fold timer per pace. The
steady fold is 100 ms; the live fold is 34 ms. The timer batches the stale site
set for that pace, increments the shared site-version counter once, and
notifies stale listeners. `state.set` is special: after updating the value it
flushes both steady and live folds immediately. Plugin `ui.invalidate` has its
own 100 ms steady / 34 ms live pacing; live delivery depends on an active
interactive site and is suppressed for a plugin recently marked slow.

For drawing, `jBr.uiRender` computes `Lue(site)` before starting `FBr`. `FBr`
executes the hook chain and commits the read set after completion. The Client
fault registry starts its snapshot before `uiRender`; after the result it
records the validated Client rows against a recomputed current signature.
Cache reuse checks the stored composite signature against a fresh `Lue(site)`.
Thus the relevant comparisons are at draw start, commit/record, and later
reuse; the source does not define the Host's token wire encoding.

The separate terminal viewport producer debounces column changes by 100 ms
and updates `ui.render viewport`. `Rh` excludes that key, so it must not be
substituted for the global `Fv` input.

## Host mapping and remaining gap

The Harness Host now carries a global Client render-generation input alongside
its committed state dependencies and matched-plugin versions. A successful
`ModHost` load/replacement advances it once; unload advances it at removal
start and again after a successful worker reply and local cleanup. Each
committed Client site folds a changed global generation into its numeric
`client_state_token` when the token is observed at render start, render finish,
or fault dispatch. Global bumps also invalidate all currently committed
Client sites, including sites whose matching plugin list did not change.
The actual Orchestrator `CwdChangedFirer` calls this Host input after the
working-directory change and CwdChanged hook dispatch.
Load failure before a successful worker reply does not bump. An unload that
fails after removal-start keeps its first bump and does not make the
post-response bump.

The current Mod Host has no automatic main Hooks-worker respawn path: a process
exit surfaces as `worker exited`, so Native `sBt` has no Host lifecycle event
to map yet. Do not use Client worker remount epochs or ordinary render
revisions as substitutes. The CwdChanged wiring covers the existing shell
working-directory event path; it does not prove that the separate Native CLI
directory-rehome command is implemented end to end.

The probe is static source evidence only. It does not execute Native plugin
load/reload, cwd change, terminal rendering, or Desktop surface transport.
